<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919374_theRebbe_640" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919374_theRebbe_640__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar explains that the world was created for the sake of Israel and the Torah, and that the purpose of creation is for Israel to study Torah specifically in this lower world.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And the maamar of the Baal HaGeulah continues,</t>
    <t s="2">(after explaining the two matters of prayer and Torah),</t>
    <t s="3">that the creation of the world is for the sake of Israel and for the sake of the Torah,</t>
    <t s="4">as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="5">"In the beginning, G-d created [the heavens and the earth],"</t>
    <t s="6">"In the beginning" is [an expression of] two "firsts,"</t>
    <t s="7">that the creation of the world is for the sake of Israel, who are called "first," and for the sake of the Torah, which is called "first."</t>
    <t s="8">That the intention of the creation of the world is that Israel should study the Torah as it was given below, specifically in this physical world.</t>
    <t s="9">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="10">that the connection of the two "firsts"—Israel and Torah—to what was explained previously regarding the matter of prayer and Torah,</t>
    <t s="11">is,</t>
    <t s="12">that prayer is the service and self-nullification of man</t>
    <t s="13">(Israel),</t>
    <t s="14">and therefore the two matters of prayer and Torah correspond to the two "firsts"—Israel and Torah.</t>
    <t s="15">And what the maamar says, "that Israel should study the Torah,"</t>
    <t s="16">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="17">that the matter of prayer is an elevation from below to above</t>
    <t s="18">(departure from the world),</t>
    <t s="19">and the intention of the creation of the world is that the revelation of G-dliness be drawn down into the world,</t>
    <t s="20">therefore,</t>
    <t s="21">when it speaks about the matter of the intention of the creation of the world,</t>
    <t s="22">it also says regarding Israel, "that Israel should study the Torah."</t>
    <t s="23">And based on this, we can also explain what the maamar brings</t>
    <t s="24">(in continuation of the matter that the intention of the creation of the world is that Israel should study the Torah)</t>
    <t s="25">that which our sages, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="26">"The Holy One, blessed be He, made a condition with the act of Creation: if Israel fulfills My Torah, [then the world will endure]...,"</t>
    <t s="27">and he explains,</t>
    <t s="28">that "Israel will fulfill My Torah" is the observance of the commandments</t>
    <t s="29">[and the expression "Israel will fulfill My Torah" is,</t>
    <t s="30">because the observance of the commandments must be specifically according to the Torah],</t>
    <t s="31">for this—that the world was created for the sake of the Torah—is</t>
    <t s="32">(in the language of the maamar)</t>
    <t s="33">that all matters of the world should be according to the Torah,</t>
    <t s="34">and the effect of the Torah in the world is through the observance of the Torah's commandments.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>After explaining creation's purpose, the maamar discusses the superiority of communal Torah study over individual study, and how the drawing down through Torah surpasses that of prayer, fulfilling the ultimate intent of a dwelling place in the lower worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, after the maamar explains that the creation of the world is for the sake of Israel and for the sake of the Torah, and that the sustenance of the world is through the observance of the Torah's commandments,</t>
    <t s="2">the maamar continues</t>
    <t s="3">with an explanation of the difference between the study of Torah by an individual and the study of Torah by the many,</t>
    <t s="4">that through the Torah of the many, a higher light is drawn down,</t>
    <t s="5">and he adds,</t>
    <t s="6">that this is understood a fortiori from the fact that through the prayer of the many, the drawing down is incomparably greater than the elevation.</t>
    <t s="7">And from the order of the matters in the maamar, it is implied,</t>
    <t s="8">that this—that the lesson that the drawing down through Torah [is greater] than the drawing down through prayer is in a manner of a fortiori,</t>
    <t s="9">is connected to what was explained previously regarding the matter of the intention of the creation of the world.</t>
    <t s="10">And the explanation of this can be said,</t>
    <t s="11">that the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds is that the making of the dwelling</t>
    <t s="12">(the drawing down of the revelation of G-dliness into the world)</t>
    <t s="13">should be through man.</t>
    <t s="14">And since the service of prayer is an elevation from below to above,</t>
    <t s="15">and the drawing down through prayer is from the aspect of Above, except that it comes through prayer</t>
    <t s="16">(the service of man),</t>
    <t s="17">therefore, there is an advantage in the drawing down through Torah</t>
    <t s="18">[that man's study of Torah draws down a revelation of G-dliness into the world]</t>
    <t s="19">over the drawing down through prayer.</t>
    <t s="20">And according to what is known,</t>
    <t s="21">that the true matter of "incomparable" is specifically regarding the Awtsmoos,</t>
    <t s="22">it can be said,</t>
    <t s="23">that the matter of a drawing down that is incomparable to the elevation is primarily in the drawing down through Torah,</t>
    <t s="24">for specifically through this drawing down is the intention of a dwelling place in the lower worlds completed,</t>
    <t s="25">the intention of the Awtsmoos.</t>
    <t s="26">And based on this, we can explain the order of the matters in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="27">that this—that the lesson that the drawing down through Torah [is greater] than the drawing down through prayer is in a manner of a fortiori—comes</t>
    <t s="28">(specifically)</t>
    <t s="29">after the explanation of the intention of creation,</t>
    <t s="30">for in the drawing down through Torah there are two matters,</t>
    <t s="31">the drawing down through Torah from the aspect of the Torah's own superiority—this drawing down is lower than the drawing down through prayer</t>
    <t s="32">(as in section 3 above),</t>
    <t s="33">and the drawing down through Torah from the aspect that through it, a revelation of G-dliness is drawn down into the world through the service</t>
    <t s="34">(study)</t>
    <t s="35">of man—this drawing down is higher than the drawing down through prayer,</t>
    <t s="36">as above.</t>
    <t s="37">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="38">after the explanation of the intention of creation</t>
    <t s="39">[and that this intention is completed through the Torah],</t>
    <t s="40">he adds that the lesson of Torah over prayer is in a manner of a fortiori,</t>
    <t s="41">that there is an advantage in the drawing down of Torah over the drawing down of prayer.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The maamar connects to the discourse "Hashem is for me among my helpers," questioning the plural form of "helpers" and the request to see vengeance upon enemies, and seeks to understand the connection between these two phrases.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And we can connect this with the maamar beginning "Hashem is for me among my helpers, and I will see [vengeance] upon my enemies"</t>
    <t s="2">that the Baal HaGeulah said on the first 12th of Tammuz</t>
    <t s="3">(5687),</t>
    <t s="4">that one must understand</t>
    <t s="5">his saying "Hashem is for me among my helpers,"</t>
    <t s="6">for the implication of the language is that there are several helpers</t>
    <t s="7">("my helpers" is plural)</t>
    <t s="8">and the request is that the Holy One, blessed be He, should also be among the helpers,</t>
    <t s="9">yet all of Israel believe with simple faith that He, blessed be He, alone is the helper and savior of man in all his affairs.</t>
    <t s="10">And even more so, it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="11">that the implication of the language "Hashem is for me among my helpers" is that the main ones are the helpers (plural) and the request is that the Holy One, blessed be He, should join them.</t>
    <t s="12">Also, one must understand his saying "and I will see [vengeance] upon my enemies"</t>
    <t s="13">(that he will see vengeance upon his enemies),</t>
    <t s="14">for seemingly he should have requested that they repent and become lovers.</t>
    <t s="15">And especially since Dovid himself said,</t>
    <t s="16">"Let sins cease from the earth, and sinners [will be no more]."</t>
    <t s="17">[And even more so, it is not understood his saying "and I will see [vengeance] upon my enemies,"</t>
    <t s="18">for the sense of sight is among the most elevated of the senses,</t>
    <t s="19">to the extent that regarding the innovations that will be in the future, it is [written],</t>
    <t s="20">"And the glory of Hashem will be revealed, and all flesh will see [together]...,"</t>
    <t s="21">and similarly regarding the giving of the Torah, one of the fundamental virtues of the giving of the Torah is</t>
    <t s="22">"You have been shown to know [that Hashem, He is G-d]...,"</t>
    <t s="23">and nevertheless Dovid requested "and I will see [vengeance] upon my enemies,"</t>
    <t s="24">that his sight should be upon the vengeance of his enemies].</t>
    <t s="25">Also, one must understand the connection of "and I will see [vengeance] upon my enemies" to "Hashem is for me among my helpers."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
